$f(x, y, z, w) = x^4+y^4+z^4+w^4 - 8(x^3+y^3+z^3+w^3)$
$g_1(x, y, z, w) = x+y+z+w - 12 = 0$
$g_2(x, y, z, w) = x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2 - 48 = 0$

The Lagrangian is:
$L = f(x, y, z, w) - \lambda_1 g_1(x, y, z, w) - \lambda_2 g_2(x, y, z, w)$

Next, I compute the partial derivative with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{\partial L}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} - \lambda_1 \frac{\partial g_1}{\partial x} - \lambda_2 \frac{\partial g_2}{\partial x} = 0$$

Calculating the components:
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial x} = 4x^3 - 8(3x^2) = 4x^3 - 24x^2$$
$$\frac{\partial g_1}{\partial x} = 1$$
$$\frac{\partial g_2}{\partial x} = 2x$$

Substituting these into the equation:
$$4x^3 - 24x^2 - \lambda_1(1) - \lambda_2(2x) = 0$$

Rearranging gives the necessary condition for $x$:
$$4x^3 - 24x^2 - 2\lambda_2 x = \lambda_1$$

Due to the symmetry of $f, g_1, g_2$ in $x, y, z, w$, the same equation must hold for $y, z,$ and $w$:
$$4y^3 - 24y^2 - 2\lambda_2 y = \lambda_1$$
$$4z^3 - 24z^2 - 2\lambda_2 z = \lambda_1$$
$$4w^3 - 24w^2 - 2\lambda_2 w = \lambda_1$$

This implies that $x, y, z, w$ must all be roots of the same cubic equation in $t$:
$$4t^3 - 24t^2 - 2\lambda_2 t - \lambda_1 = 0$$

I will now write this analysis into the shared notes.
